Unauthenticated POST to 9router /api/tunnel/tailscale-install (CVE-2026-59800 auth bypass) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound POST requests to the 9router route /api/tunnel/tailscale-install, which is absent from the dashboard middleware matcher and therefore reaches the handler with no cookie/JWT/CLI-token check. Any external hit on this endpoint is an exploitation attempt for the unauthenticated RCE, since this route is only ever driven by the local dashboard. Rationale: The exact route path /api/tunnel/tailscale-install and its absence from the src/proxy.js matcher are the article's core auth-bypass fact; any POST to it is exploitation. Defender query surfaces external hosts reaching the 9router listener on port 20128 (EXPOSE 20128 in the PoC) as a supporting exposure signal since Defender lacks L7 URI visibility. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/9router/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p/ • https://cve.threatint.eu/CVE/CVE-2026-59800
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized operator installing Tailscale through the 9router dashboard UI (request originates from localhost/loopback, not a public IP)
  • Internal vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys) probing the CVE-2026-59800 endpoint
  • Automated uptime/health monitor mis-configured to POST to the tunnel path
  • Security team running the published PoC in a sanctioned test
  • DAST/CI security pipeline exercising the API surface
Suppression filter
| where not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SourceIP is external/non-loopback and capture the full request; check whether the 9router host runs Node as root (docker inspect / systemd unit User=) which turns this into remote root. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the proxy, take the 9router instance offline or restrict /api/tunnel/* at the reverse proxy, and upgrade 9router to >=0.4.44. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2/UC3 on the same host for node->sudo -S sh spawns and curl fetches of tailscale.com/install.sh in the seconds after the POST to determine if code executed.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 20128
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "9router"
| summarize Conns = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Ports = make_set(LocalPort) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Conns desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/api/tunnel/tailscale-install"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc

9router (node) process spawning 'sudo -S sh' — CVE-2026-59800 command injection primitive AIExploitation High
Detects the 9router Node process spawning 'sudo -S sh', the exact child process the vulnerable installTailscaleLinux routine creates and into whose stdin the attacker-controlled sudoPassword is written. A Node/9router parent spawning a password-fed root shell is the execution primitive of the RCE. Rationale: 'sudo -S sh' spawned by a node/9router parent is taken verbatim from installTailscaleLinux in src/lib/tunnel/tailscale.js; the -S flag (read password from stdin) plus a Node parent is the article-specific fingerprint distinguishing this from interactive sudo use. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/9router/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1548.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate authenticated Tailscale install triggered through the 9router dashboard (same code path, benign stdin)
  • Other Node apps that legitimately shell out via 'sudo -S sh' with a cached password
  • Automation/CI runner that pipes install scripts through sudo -S
  • Config-management tooling wrapping sudo shells under a Node supervisor
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree and the children of the sh process — a legitimate install shows apt-get/curl/tailscaled; injection shows recon (id/whoami), file writes to /tmp, or network tools, and Tailscale never actually installs. Check InitiatingProcessId lineage back to the 9router listener. 2) Contain: kill the node/sh process tree, isolate the host, rotate any secrets reachable as the 9router user (root if containerized), upgrade to >=0.4.44. 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 (a preceding unauthenticated POST) and UC3 (curl fetch of tailscale.com/install.sh) within the same PID lineage; sweep other 9router hosts for the same node->sudo->sh pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "sudo"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("-S","sh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "9router"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has "sudo"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_all ("-S","sh")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs","9router") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "9router"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessId, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

9router chain: node fetches tailscale.com/install.sh then spawns sudo -S sh within seconds AIExploitation High
Correlates the two-stage exploitation chain: the 9router Node process spawning curl/wget to fetch https://tailscale.com/install.sh, immediately followed (same parent PID, <=10s) by a 'sudo -S sh' spawn. Tying both events to the same node parent PID confirms the CVE-2026-59800 fetch-then-pipe-to-root-shell sequence rather than either half in isolation. Rationale: Both the curl fetch of tailscale.com/install.sh and the sudo -S sh spawn are the exact code path in tailscale.js; joining on the shared node parent PID within seconds captures the full attack chain and drops either half occurring alone, giving a low-FP alert. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/9router/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized Tailscale install via the 9router dashboard executes the identical fetch+sudo sequence (benign) — treat as TP-worthy only when no authorized change window matches
  • Operator manually re-running the install through the app during troubleshooting
  • Blue-team detonation of the CVE PoC in a lab
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the fetch and sudo events share the node parent PID and occurred within seconds; inspect whether the sh child ran install.sh's expected commands or exited early (the '; exit 0' injection kills sh before tailscaled installs). Check for a preceding unauthenticated POST (UC1). 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the process tree, rotate credentials accessible to the 9router/root user, upgrade to >=0.4.44. 3) Hunt: enumerate all children spawned by the sh process for dropped files, reverse shells, or new persistence; sweep the fleet for other 9router hosts exhibiting the same fetch->sudo chain.
let Window = 10s;
let Fetches = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("curl","wget")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "tailscale.com/install.sh"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "9router"
    | project FetchTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, NodeParentId = InitiatingProcessId, FetchCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "sudo"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("-S","sh")
| join kind=inner Fetches on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (FetchTime .. FetchTime + Window)
| where InitiatingProcessId == NodeParentId
| project FetchTime, SudoTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, FetchTime), NodeParentId, FetchCmd, SudoCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by SudoTime desc
let Window = 10s;
let Fetches = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","wget")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has "tailscale.com/install.sh"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs","9router") or ParentProcessCommandLine has "9router"
    | project FetchTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, NodeParentId = ParentProcessId, FetchCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine;

| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_all ("-S","sh")

| where TimeGenerated between (FetchTime .. FetchTime + Window)

| order by SudoTime desc

curl/wget child of 9router node fetching tailscale.com/install.sh (probe or exploit delivery) AIDelivery Medium
Flags the outbound fetch of tailscale.com/install.sh by a curl/wget process whose parent is the 9router Node process. Per the advisory, this fetch fires on every hit to the endpoint — including hardened hosts where the sudo step later fails — so it surfaces both successful exploitation and reconnaissance/probing of CVE-2026-59800. Rationale: The article states the endpoint always triggers 'an outbound fetch from tailscale.com' even when RCE fails, making curl/wget->tailscale.com/install.sh with a node parent a reliable probe indicator; parent=node distinguishes it from a human running the official install command in a shell. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6g7-pvmx-m74p • https://cve.threatint.eu/CVE/CVE-2026-59800
ATT&CKT1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized Tailscale install through the 9router dashboard (parent is genuinely node and the fetch is legitimate)
  • Administrator running the official 'curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh' from a shell (parent would be bash/sh, excluded by the node-parent filter)
  • Container image build step pre-installing Tailscale under a node entrypoint
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router")
Response runbook
1) Triage: determine if a matching unauthenticated POST (UC1) preceded the fetch and whether a sudo -S sh spawn (UC2/UC3) followed on the same host/PID — fetch-only with no sudo success suggests a probe against a hardened host. 2) Contain: if paired with sudo execution, isolate and treat as compromise; otherwise restrict /api/tunnel/* at the proxy and prioritize the upgrade to >=0.4.44. 3) Hunt: aggregate source IPs of the inbound POSTs across all 9router hosts to identify a scanning campaign (Shadowserver reported in-the-wild exploitation from 2026-07-04).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl endswith "tailscale.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router")
| summarize Fetches = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl
| order by Fetches desc

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl endswith "tailscale.com"

| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node","nodejs","9router")
| summarize Fetches = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl
| order by Fetches desc

Mautic vulnerable to Path Traversal via Campaign Import

ATT&CKT1190

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Mautic campaign import ZIP upload — POST to campaign import endpoint
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web-server process writes PHP file into Mautic config/cache/media/logs (zip-slip landing)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] HTTP request to an executable PHP file under Mautic /media (web-shell interaction)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Web-server process writes PHP file into Mautic config/cache/media/logs (zip-slip landing) AIInstallation High
Hunts the core of CVE-2026-9559: the Mautic campaign-import ZIP extraction escaping the temp directory and dropping an attacker-controlled .php/.phtml/.phar into Symfony's config, var/cache, var/logs or media trees, executed under the web-server user (php-fpm/apache/nginx). A web-server process writing executable PHP into these directories at request time is almost never legitimate outside a controlled cache warm-up. Rationale: Keys on the article's concrete outcome — 'write arbitrary PHP files to sensitive system directories … overwrite critical internal configuration or cache components' — using Mautic 7's real Symfony layout (config/, var/cache, var/logs, media) plus the web-server process identity that owns the write. Corroborated against NVD and the Mautic 7.1.2 release; the Symfony compiled-container exclusion removes the one high-volume legitimate PHP-into-cache writer. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-6r9h-4h75-7q4x • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9559 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mautic/core/CVE-2026-9559/ • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/releases/tag/7.1.2
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Symfony cache warm-up writing compiled container/service PHP into /var/cache/prod/ on first request or after `bin/console cache:clear`
  • Mautic plugin/theme installation via the admin UI writing PHP assets into media or plugin dirs
  • In-place Mautic upgrade / Composer operation regenerating cached PHP
  • Backup-restore tooling repopulating var/cache from a snapshot
  • Developer or deploy script running as the web user during a controlled release window
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has "/var/cache/" and (FileName startswith "Container" or FileName endswith "ProjectContainer.php" or FileName startswith "srcApp_Kernel" or FileName matches regex @"get[A-Za-z0-9_]+Service\.php$")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cache:warmup","cache:clear","assets:install"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the exact FolderPath/FileName and SHA256, and read the dropped file — attacker webshells contain eval/system/base64_decode/assert; legitimate Symfony cache files are compiled container/service classes. Confirm whether a campaign import ran on this host within the prior 5 minutes. 2) Contain: isolate the Mautic host or block inbound HTTP; quarantine the dropped PHP; revoke campaign:imports:create from all non-admin users and rotate the app secret/DB creds if the file is a shell. 3) Hunt: pivot on the web-server user for subsequent shell spawns and outbound connections, enumerate every .php written under config/var/cache/var/logs/media in the last 30 days, and confirm the instance is patched to Mautic 7.1.2.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar" or FileName endswith ".pht" or FileName endswith ".php5" or FileName endswith ".php7"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/config/","/var/cache/","/var/logs/","/media/")
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "php-fpm" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd","apache2","nginx","php","php8"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
// drop Symfony's legitimate compiled-container cache writes
| where not (FolderPath has "/var/cache/" and (FileName startswith "Container" or FileName endswith "ProjectContainer.php" or FileName startswith "srcApp_Kernel"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phtml","phar","pht","php5","php7")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/config/","/var/cache/","/var/logs/","/media/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| where not (TargetFilePath has "/var/cache/" and (TargetFileName startswith "Container" or TargetFileName endswith "ProjectContainer.php" or TargetFileName startswith "srcApp_Kernel"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Web Server Process Writes PHP File into Mautic Config or Cache Directory
id: b7e4c2a1-3f6d-4a9c-8e21-7d5f0a1b2c3d
status: experimental
description: Detects a web-server process (php-fpm/apache/nginx) writing an executable PHP file into a Mautic Symfony config, var/cache, var/logs or media directory, consistent with the CVE-2026-9559 campaign-import path-traversal RCE.
references:
  - https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-6r9h-4h75-7q4x
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9559
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/09
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-fpm8.1'
      - '/php-fpm8.2'
      - '/php-fpm8.3'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
  selection_dir:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/config/'
      - '/var/cache/'
      - '/var/logs/'
      - '/media/'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phar'
      - '.pht'
  filter_symfony:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/var/cache/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: 'ProjectContainer.php'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_dir and selection_ext and not filter_symfony
level: high
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|httpd|apache2|nginx)/i
| TargetFileName=/\/(config|var\/cache|var\/logs|media)\/.*\.(php|phtml|phar|pht|php5|php7)$/i
| NOT (TargetFileName=/\/var\/cache\/.*(Container|ProjectContainer)\.php$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) (Filesystem.file_path="*/config/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/cache/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/logs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/media/*") (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.pht" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php7") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","php-fpm7.4","httpd","apache2","nginx","php") | where NOT (like(file_path,"%/var/cache/%") AND (like(file_name,"Container%") OR like(file_name,"%ProjectContainer.php") OR like(file_name,"srcApp_Kernel%Container.php"))) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified) (Filesystem.file_path="*/config/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/cache/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/logs/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/media/*") (Filesystem.file_name="*.php" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phtml" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.phar" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.pht" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php5" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.php7") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","php-fpm8.3","php-fpm7.4","httpd","apache2","nginx","php") | where NOT (like(file_path,"%/var/cache/%") AND (like(file_name,"Container%") OR like(file_name,"%ProjectContainer.php") OR like(file_name,"srcApp_Kernel%Container.php"))) | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Mautic campaign import ZIP upload — POST to campaign import endpoint AIDelivery Medium
Surfaces the delivery step of CVE-2026-9559: an authenticated POST to the Mautic campaign-import route carrying the malicious ZIP. Hunting-tier because import is a legitimate feature; pivot on the source user/IP and correlate against a PHP file-write (UC1) on the same host within ~60s to promote to a confirmed exploit. Rationale: Grounded on the article's named privilege/feature (campaign:imports:create, 'campaign import feature', ZIP upload) confirmed as a Mautic 7 REST feature accepting ZIP form-data. Alone it is a legitimate action, so it is scoped as a hunt whose value is the source-actor pivot and correlation with UC1's PHP write. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-6r9h-4h75-7q4x • https://devdocs.mautic.org/en/5.x/rest_api/campaigns.html • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mautic/core/CVE-2026-9559/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing admin legitimately importing a campaign template exported from another Mautic instance
  • Migration/onboarding project bulk-importing campaigns during a cutover window
  • CI/CD or IaC tooling restoring campaign definitions from a repo
  • Vendor/consultant importing a packaged campaign bundle
  • Automated backup-restore re-importing campaign archives
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the SrcUsername/SrcIpAddr and check whether this account has ever performed a campaign import before and whether campaign:imports:create was recently granted; verify the source IP is within the IT-admin/marketing range. 2) Contain: if the actor is new/unexpected, disable the account, revoke campaign:imports:create org-wide, and preserve the uploaded ZIP for analysis. 3) Hunt: correlate this import timestamp against UC1 PHP file-writes on the Mautic host within 60s and against any web-server shell spawn; if a drop is found, treat as confirmed RCE and escalate.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "campaigns/import" or Url has "campaign/import"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST (Web.url="*campaigns/import*" OR Web.url="*campaign/import*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST (Web.url="*campaigns/import*" OR Web.url="*campaign/import*") by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
HTTP request to an executable PHP file under Mautic /media (web-shell interaction) AICommand & Control High
Detects the execution/command channel after CVE-2026-9559: an HTTP request that reaches a .php/.phtml/.phar under Mautic's web-accessible /media path (which should only ever serve static assets) and returns 200, indicating the dropped web shell was invoked. Distinct pivot from the file-write (UC1) — this fires on the web-access log even if endpoint telemetry is absent. Rationale: The article's RCE outcome lands PHP into config/cache/media; only /media is web-reachable, and Mautic serves it as a static-asset store, so any PHP under /media returning 200 is a web-shell invocation — a clean, high-fidelity signal that needs no threshold. Scoped to 200/500 to drop scanner 404 noise. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-6r9h-4h75-7q4x • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9559 • https://securityonline.info/mautic-security-vulnerabilities-rce/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanner / pentest probing for web shells under /media (usually 404, excluded by the 200/500 filter)
  • Legitimate Mautic plugin that intentionally serves a PHP endpoint from a media/asset path (rare, allowlist it)
  • Developer leaving a phpinfo/test file in media during troubleshooting
  • WAF or CDN health-check hitting an asset URL that happens to include .php in a query string
  • Misrouted request where .php appears only in the query parameter, not the path (regex anchors on path extension to avoid this)
Suppression filter
| search NOT Web.url="*/media/js/*" NOT Web.url="*/media/css/*" NOT http_user_agent="*HealthCheck*"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the requested file on disk and the surrounding access-log entries for the same SrcIpAddr — POST bodies, repeated requests, and command-like query strings confirm a shell; capture the User-Agent and IP. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF/edge, remove the PHP file from /media, isolate the host, and rotate web-app and DB credentials. 3) Hunt: enumerate all PHP under /media and other Mautic dirs, pivot the web-server user for spawned shells and outbound C2, and trace back to the UC2 campaign-import request and the UC1 file-write to reconstruct the full chain; confirm patch to 7.1.2.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "/media/"
| where Url matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|pht|php5|php7)(\?|$)"
| where HttpStatusCode in ("200","500")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Web.http_method) as http_methods min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/media/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/media/*.phtml*" OR Web.url="*/media/*.phar*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Web.http_method) as http_methods min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*/media/*.php*" OR Web.url="*/media/*.phtml*" OR Web.url="*/media/*.phar*") Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Mautic Twig SSTI RCE: PHP/web process spawns OS shell (CVE-2026-9558) AIExploitation High
Hunts the post-exploitation observable of CVE-2026-9558 — a Mautic web-tier process (php-fpm, php-cgi, apache2/httpd/nginx worker, or w3wp) directly spawning an interactive shell or recon binary. In a healthy Mautic install the PHP runtime never forks /bin/sh or whoami; when it does, an uploaded Twig theme has broken the sandbox and reached OS-command execution. Rationale: Grounded in Mautic's confirmed PHP/Symfony/Twig stack (advisory + GitLab/NVD) — the vuln renders theme Twig without a sandbox, so successful exploitation manifests as the PHP runtime forking a shell, which never happens in a benign Mautic web request. Parent(php/apache/nginx/w3wp)->child(shell/recon) is the highest-fidelity RCE pivot available without article-supplied hashes. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-9558 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mautic/core/CVE-2026-9558/ • https://www.thehackerwire.com/mautic-critical-ssti-cve-2026-9558-allows-rce/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Mautic scheduled tasks (php bin/console mautic:segments:update / mautic:emails:send) spawning sh for symfony process helpers
  • Composer/deployment scripts run as the web user invoking shell hooks during an upgrade
  • PDF/preview generation plugins shelling out to wkhtmltopdf or imagemagick's convert
  • Admin using a web-based file manager or terminal plugin on the same PHP-FPM pool
  • Monitoring/backup agents that exec via the PHP-FPM worker (e.g. New Relic, healthcheck shellouts)
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildCmd has "bin/console" or ChildCmd has_any ("wkhtmltopdf","wkhtmltoimage","convert -","composer") or ParentCmd has "bin/console")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ChildCmd and ParentCmd — a legit Symfony console task references 'bin/console'; an attacker command runs whoami/id/curl to an external host or reads /etc/passwd or Mautic's app/config/local.php. Confirm the acting host runs Mautic and check its version against 7.1.2/6.0.9/5.2.11/4.4.20. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the child process tree, and revoke sessions/API tokens for any Mautic user holding core:themes:create; block outbound to any C2 seen in the child cmdline. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName for UC2 (new .twig under themes/), review Mautic audit log for recent theme installs, and sweep for dropped web shells or cron persistence written by the PHP user.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "php" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","whoami","id","uname","curl","wget","python","python3","perl")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "php" or ParentProcessName has_any ("httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","cmd.exe","powershell","whoami","/id","uname","curl","wget","python","perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mautic Twig SSTI RCE - Web Process Spawns OS Shell (CVE-2026-9558)
id: 6b2e1c9a-4f3d-4a17-9c2e-7d8f1a0b3e21
description: Detects a Mautic PHP/web-server process spawning an interactive shell or recon binary, the post-exploitation signature of the Twig theme-template SSTI in CVE-2026-9558.
references:

Weaponized Twig theme written under Mautic themes/ by web process (CVE-2026-9558) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the delivery step of CVE-2026-9558 — the Mautic web tier (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) writing a .twig template into the themes/ directory, i.e. an uploaded/created theme landing on disk. Pairs with the RCE detection: a fresh web-written theme template followed by a PHP-spawned shell on the same host is the full SSTI chain. Rationale: Mautic docs confirm themes are self-contained dirs under themes/ holding *.html.twig files, installed by uploading a zip through the web UI — so the payload physically lands as a web-process-written .twig. Scoping the writer to the PHP/web runtime (not an admin's editor) separates exploit-driven writes from developer file edits and gives a clean pivot to correlate with the UC1 shell spawn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mautic/mautic/security/advisories/GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg • https://docs.mautic.org/en/5.2/builders/creating_themes.html • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mautic/core/CVE-2026-9558/
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate administrator installing or updating a theme zip via Settings > Themes
  • Mautic version upgrade repopulating bundled themes (blank, cards, nature, etc.) into themes/
  • Marketing/design team uploading a custom corporate email/page theme
  • CI/CD or deployment automation syncing theme directories as the web user
  • Theme builder saving edits to email.html.twig / page.html.twig from the UI
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which Mautic user triggered the write via the app audit log (Settings > Audit Log) and correlate the timestamp with the FolderPath; a new theme folder name you don't recognize, or a modified base/page/email .twig on an internet-facing host, is suspicious. Grab and read the .twig content for SSTI markers (_self.env, registerUndefinedFilterCallback, getFilter, system/exec/passthru/proc_open). 2) Contain: quarantine the theme file, revoke core:themes:create from the acting user pending review, and confirm the host is on a patched build (7.1.2/6.0.9/5.2.11/4.4.20). 3) Hunt: run UC1 on the same DeviceName for a php-spawned shell within minutes of the write, and review web/access logs for the theme-install POST and subsequent theme-preview/render requests.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has "/themes/" and FileName endswith ".twig"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "php" or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/themes/" and TargetFileName endswith ".twig"
| where ActingProcessName has "php" or ActingProcessName has_any ("httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Affected zebrad (<= v4.4.1) exposure to P2SH sigop consensus-split (CVE-2026-52735) AIExploitation High
Surfaces hosts with an installed Zebra/zebrad build at or below v4.4.1, which undercounts P2SH sigops and can be forced into a chain split from zcashd. This is asset-exposure hunting: identify vulnerable Zcash full nodes before an attacker broadcasts malicious P2SH-spend transactions. Rationale: Uses the concrete affected boundary from the advisory (zebrad <= v4.4.1, patched in 4.4.2) and CVE-2026-52735. parse_version gives an exact vulnerable-version test; SoftwareName 'zebrad' avoids collision with unrelated Zebra Technologies printer software. Note: GHSA-2prc-cj5x-4443 later found the 4.4.2 fix incomplete, so 4.5.1 is the true-safe floor. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-gf9r-m956-97qx • https://zfnd.org/zebra-4-5-1-security-fixes/ • https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-2prc-cj5x-4443 • https://dailycve.com/zebra-consensus-divergence-critical/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Zebra Technologies label-printer / barcode driver software matching the 'zebra' string (mitigated by SoftwareName 'zebrad' filter)
  • Decommissioned or lab-only Zcash test nodes that never touch mainnet consensus
  • Host already upgraded but vuln scanner holding a stale software-inventory record
  • Vulnerability scanner mis-mapping a different Zebra advisory to this CVE
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVendor !has "Zebra Technologies" and SoftwareName !has "printer"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host actually runs a validating full node (not just an installed binary) and note the exact SoftwareVersion — anything < 4.4.2 is exposed to CVE-2026-52735. 2) Contain: schedule upgrade to a patched build; because the 4.4.2 fix was found incomplete (GHSA-2prc-cj5x-4443), upgrade straight to >= 4.5.1. Until patched, monitor the node's chain tip against a reference zcashd node for divergence. 3) Hunt: enumerate all zebrad hosts via inventory, and pivot to UC 'zebrad node process execution' and the 'bad-blk-sigops' log hunt to see whether an exploit block was already accepted.

| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, EndOfSupportStatus
| order by Timestamp desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc

zebrad node process execution at vulnerable version (CVE-2026-52735) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts live execution of the zebrad binary and surfaces its product version so analysts can confirm exposure to the P2SH sigop-undercount consensus split. Complements inventory-based detection by catching nodes launched from non-packaged paths (source builds, containers) that TVM may miss. Rationale: Anchors on the exact binary name 'zebrad' from the advisory and surfaces ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion so analysts can read the version off Windows builds; Linux builds (no version info) are still surfaced rather than dropped. Distinct pivot from the TVM inventory UC — catches source/container launches inventory misses. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-gf9r-m956-97qx • https://zfnd.org/zebra-4-5-1-security-fixes/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate zebrad node operators running an already-patched build (>= 4.5.1) — version column disambiguates on Windows
  • CI/CD or automated test harnesses repeatedly spawning zebrad
  • Container orchestration restarting zebrad pods (high event volume, benign)
  • Linux hosts where product-version metadata is empty, forcing manual version confirmation
Suppression filter
| where isempty(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion) or parse_version(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion) < parse_version("4.4.2")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion; if empty (typical on Linux), query the node RPC/`zebrad --version` to get the build. Versions < 4.4.2 are exposed. 2) Contain: for exposed validating nodes, plan upgrade to >= 4.5.1 (the 4.4.2 patch was incomplete) and watch the chain tip vs a reference zcashd. 3) Hunt: for every host seen running zebrad, run the 'bad-blk-sigops' log-reject hunt and cross-check the inventory UC to build the full affected-asset list.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "zebrad" or FileName =~ "zebrad.exe"
| where isempty(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion) or parse_version(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion) < parse_version("4.4.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has "zebrad"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team detonating the lure URL in a sandbox/SOAR enrichment from a corporate endpoint
  • Threat-intel analyst manually browsing to pamconj.com during investigation
  • Web proxy/URL-scanner appliance pre-fetching the domain for categorization
  • DNS sinkhole or RPZ appliance logging the blocked query (benign but noisy)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user/device and confirm whether the connection was a live browser navigation (device-code lure) vs automated scanner; pull the referring email/Teams message for the same recipient. 2) Contain: block all *.pamconj.com and the workers.dev lure at proxy/DNS; if a real user reached the device-code page, revoke that user's refresh tokens/sessions (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken) and force re-auth. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (new Entra device registration for that user) and UC3 (inbox-rule creation) within 24h; review that user's SigninLogs for device-code grants from unfamiliar IPs.

Entra ID device registration = ARToken PRT persistence after device-code token theft AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the ARToken/EvilTokens persistence step: after stealing a refresh token via device-code phishing, the operator registers a new device in Entra ID to obtain a Primary Refresh Token for durable SSO that survives password resets. Surfaces device add/register/join audit events with the acting user, source IP and target device for rapid correlation to a suspicious sign-in. Rationale: Grounded in the article's explicit 'Primary Refresh Token (PRT) persistence' capability and corroborated by Sekoia/Microsoft describing refresh-token-driven device registration in Entra ID. Device add/register audit operations are the concrete, queryable footprint of that step; Falcon/CloudWatch left empty because Entra ID audit isn't in FDR or CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/new-widespread-eviltokens-kit-device-code-phishing-as-a-service-part-1/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/06/ai-enabled-device-code-phishing-campaign-april-2026/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/microsoft-365-phishing-panel-uses-oauth-device-code-flow/
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1528
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user enrolling a new phone/laptop into Intune/Entra (BYOD or refresh cycle)
  • Autopilot/Intune bulk device provisioning by IT during onboarding
  • Windows Hello for Business device registration on password change
  • Service desk registering a replacement device for a user
Suppression filter
| where ActorIp !in ("<intune_provisioning_egress_ip>")  // NOTE: replace only if you maintain a known Intune egress allowlist; otherwise correlate ActorIp against SigninLogs device-code/foreign-IP sign-ins
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each registration confirm the actor UPN, source IP and device name; check whether the user's most recent sign-in was a device-code grant or came from an unfamiliar/foreign IP within the prior hour. 2) Contain: if unattributable, disable/remove the newly registered device, revoke the user's refresh tokens and PRTs (Revoke-AzureADUserAllRefreshToken + session invalidation), and require MFA re-registration. 3) Hunt: enumerate all devices registered by the same actor IP across the tenant, review SharePoint/OneDrive mass-download and inbox-rule creation (UC3) for the affected mailbox.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("Add registered owner to device","Add registered users to device","Register device","Add device")
| extend Ip = tostring(IPAddress)
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, Ip, CountryCode, City, ObjectName, ObjectType
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName in ("Add registered owner to device","Add registered users to device","Register device","Add device","Update device")
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ActorIp = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Actor, ActorIp, TargetDevice, Result, ResultReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ARToken BEC toolkit: inbox forwarding/hiding rule creation on compromised M365 mailbox AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the ARToken/EvilTokens post-compromise BEC action: automated creation of inbox rules that forward/redirect mail externally and delete or move messages to hide attacker activity. Targets mailbox audit events for New/Set-InboxRule carrying forwarding or delete/move parameters. Rationale: Directly targets ARToken's documented BEC capability ('inbox rule creation for forwarding and deleting messages') via the exact Exchange audit operations and forwarding/delete parameters. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch empty because M365 mailbox audit isn't shipped to those platforms in this tenant. Cross-checked against: • https://cyberscoop.com/artoken-bec-platform-cisco-talos/ • https://gbhackers.com/eviltokens-linked-artoken-panel/
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1564.008
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately setting up out-of-office/auto-forward to a personal or delegate mailbox
  • Admin-configured transport/journaling rule mistaken for a user inbox rule
  • Power-user creating a 'move to folder' organization rule for newsletters
  • Migration tooling recreating rules during a mailbox move
Suppression filter
| where Params !has "@yourcorpdomain.com"  // keep only rules forwarding/redirecting OUTSIDE the org; internal delegate forwarding is common and low-risk
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the rule forwards/redirects to an EXTERNAL domain or deletes/moves security-alert mail; check the ClientIP/country against the user's normal sign-in pattern and recent device-code sign-ins. 2) Contain: delete the malicious rule, revoke the user's tokens and PRTs, reset credentials, and block the external forwarding destination at the mail gateway. 3) Hunt: correlate to UC1 (infra contact) and UC2 (new device registration) for the same user; search for identical rule names/forwarding targets across other mailboxes to scope the BEC blast radius.

| where RawEventData has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage","MoveToFolder")
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity

| where Params has_any ("ForwardTo","ForwardAsAttachmentTo","RedirectTo","DeleteMessage","MoveToFolder")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, Params, OfficeWorkload
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

CVE-2026-50027 unauthenticated write to mcp-memory-service /api/documents/upload AIInstallation High
Hunts successful POSTs to mcp-memory-service /api/documents/upload or /batch-upload that carry no Authorization/API-key header, indicating the CVE-2026-50027 auth-bypass being exercised to inject attacker-controlled content (memory poisoning / prompt-injection surface). Article-specific because it targets the exact vulnerable routes that lack Depends(require_write_access). Rationale: Uses the article's exact vulnerable routes (/api/documents/upload, /api/documents/batch-upload) and the discriminator that a legitimate client under MCP_API_KEY/OAuth would send an Authorization header the server ignores, so an absent header + 200 fingerprints the bypass. Corroborated against the GitLab advisory (fixed 10.67.1). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCP client that genuinely does not send an Authorization header because the operator never enabled MCP_API_KEY/OAuth (auth disabled deployments)
  • Internal automation/backup jobs that upload documents from a trusted subnet without headers
  • Load-balancer or reverse-proxy health probes that strip auth headers before logging
  • Security scanners / your own vuln-management team validating the CVE
  • API gateway that terminates auth upstream so the app-tier log shows no Authorization header
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("10.0.0.0/8_trusted_automation_ip") and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has "HealthProbe"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all requests from SrcIpAddr to /api/documents/* in the last 24h; confirm the deployment has MCP_API_KEY/OAuth enabled (if not, this is expected use, not attack). Inspect uploaded content via /api/documents/search-content for injected/poisoned data. 2) Contain: put the mcp-memory-service HTTP server behind auth at the proxy/WAF or take it off the public interface, and upgrade to >= 10.67.1. 3) Hunt: from the same SrcIpAddr look for follow-on DELETE /api/documents/remove-by-tags and GET /api/documents/search-content, and review the memory store for attacker-controlled entries that agents may have already consumed.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/documents/upload" or Url has "/api/documents/batch-upload"
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where toint(HttpStatusCode) == 200
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization)   // no bearer/API key sent -> MCP_API_KEY/OAuth bypassed (CVE-2026-50027)
| summarize UploadCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Urls = make_set(Url, 10) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, HttpUserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by UploadCount desc

CVE-2026-50027 unauthenticated destructive delete via /api/documents/remove-by-tags AIActions on Objectives High
Alerts on successful DELETE requests to mcp-memory-service /api/documents/remove-by-tags or /remove/{upload_id} lacking an Authorization header — the availability/integrity impact of CVE-2026-50027 where an unauthenticated attacker destroys memories created by authenticated users. Article-specific to the DELETE sinks that call storage.delete_by_tags(). Rationale: DELETE to /api/documents/remove-by-tags is the exact availability sink (storage.delete_by_tags) named in the article; DELETE against a memory store is rare and low-FP, and an absent Authorization header on a 200 confirms the unauthenticated destruction. Cross-checked with GitLab advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/

CVE-2026-50027 unauthenticated bulk read/enumeration of mcp-memory-service document store AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single source issuing a high volume of successful unauthenticated GETs to /api/documents/search-content/{upload_id} and /api/documents/history, indicating systematic enumeration and bulk exfiltration of stored memory content via CVE-2026-50027. Threshold-based to separate mass retrieval from single legitimate lookups. Rationale: Targets the article's confidentiality sinks GET /api/documents/search-content/{upload_id} and /api/documents/history; a 5-minute volume/distinct-doc threshold with no auth header captures automated iteration over upload_ids that single legitimate reads would not trip. Thresholds documented inline. Corroborated via GitLab advisory. CVE-2026-50027 auth-bypass fingerprint: 401 on /api/memories then 200 on /api/documents from same source AIExploitation High
Correlates a 401 on the properly-guarded /api/memories endpoint followed by a 200 on any /api/documents/* route from the same source IP within a short window — the exact behavioural signature of the CVE-2026-50027 PoC, where an attacker probes the auth boundary then pivots to the unguarded document API. Very high fidelity because it captures the inconsistent-auth pivot itself. Rationale: Reproduces the PoC's own attack-chain evidence (STEP 1 GET /api/memories -> 401, then STEP 4/5 /api/documents -> 200) as a same-source time-window correlation; the 401-then-200 pivot across the inconsistent auth boundary is unique to this CVE and near-zero FP. Verified against GHSA and GitLab advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/

CVE-2026-50027 full exploit chain: probe, write, bulk-read, delete from one source in 15m AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates the complete CVE-2026-50027 workflow from a single source inside 15 minutes: a 401 probe on /api/memories, a successful POST /api/documents/upload, high-volume GET reads on /api/documents/*, and a DELETE /api/documents/remove* cover-tracks step. Fires only on the end-to-end read+write+destroy pattern the advisory describes, so it is a distinct multi-stage pivot from the single-action UCs. Rationale: Encodes the article's stated end-to-end capability (write + read + delete) and the PoC's 6-step run as a single-source 15-minute chain requiring probe+write+delete stages; requiring all three destructive stages together makes it near-zero FP and distinct from the per-action UCs. Corroborated via GHSA and GitLab advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-84hp-mqvj-3p8h • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/mcp-memory-service/CVE-2026-50027/

let win = 15m;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Url has "/api/memories" or Url has "/api/documents/"
| extend Stage = case(
    Url has "/api/memories" and toint(HttpStatusCode) == 401, "probe",
    (Url has "/api/documents/upload" or Url has "/api/documents/batch-upload") and HttpMethod =~ "POST" and toint(HttpStatusCode) == 200, "write",
    (Url has "/api/documents/search-content/" or Url has "/api/documents/history") and HttpMethod =~ "GET" and toint(HttpStatusCode) == 200, "read",

| where datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen) <= 900   // 15m window
| order by LastSeen desc

Ghost x-ghost-preview cache-poisoning header in inbound HTTP requests (CVE-2026-53943) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the internal-only x-ghost-preview request header arriving at a Ghost frontend that sits behind a shared cache (Fastly/Cloudflare/nginx proxy_cache). Presence of this header from external/unexpected sources is the precondition for CVE-2026-53943 cache-poisoning XSS, where a preview-altered response gets cached and served to other visitors. Rationale: Uses the exact header token 'x-ghost-preview' named in the advisory as the sole vulnerability trigger; this header is normally emitted only by Ghost's own admin preview flow, so its appearance in shared-cache proxy logs is inherently anomalous. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty — HTTP request headers are not in EDR/CloudTrail schemas. Corroborated against GitLab Advisory DB and DailyCVE (CVSS 9.6). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Ghost editor/author using the built-in post-preview feature
  • Shared preview links opened by reviewers or marketing staff
  • CMS integration or headless-build job pre-rendering preview content
  • Synthetic monitoring / uptime checks configured to hit preview URLs
  • Internal QA automation validating draft rendering
Suppression filter
| where isempty(RequestCookies) or RequestCookies !has "ghost"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP(s) and confirm whether they belong to known editorial staff, CI/build systems, or monitoring. Check whether the same request also carried a valid Ghost session cookie (legit) or none (suspicious). 2) Contain: at the cache layer (Fastly/Cloudflare/nginx) add the documented workaround — bypass/vary cache for any request carrying x-ghost-preview — and confirm Ghost is upgraded to >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: for each poisoned URL, check whether subsequent cache-HIT responses were served to other clients, and review admin/staff logons on the frontend domain for account takeover.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ghost x-ghost-preview Cache-Poisoning Header (CVE-2026-53943)
id: 3f6c1e2a-9b4d-4c7e-8a11-2d5f7c9e4a10
status: experimental
description: Detects the internal-only x-ghost-preview request header at a Ghost frontend behind a shared cache, the precondition for CVE-2026-53943 cache-poisoning XSS.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62q6-4hv4-vjrw
  - https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'x-ghost-preview'
  condition: keywords
level: medium
source:linux.syslog "x-ghost-preview"
CLOUD
index=web OR index=proxy (sourcetype="nginx:plus:access" OR sourcetype="nginx:access" OR sourcetype="access_combined" OR sourcetype="cloudflare:json" OR sourcetype="fastly") "x-ghost-preview"
| stats count as hits, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(uri_path) as uri_path, dc(clientip) as distinct_clients by host, sourcetype, clientip
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - hits
Unauthenticated x-ghost-preview request to cached Ghost frontend (CVE-2026-53943 precondition) AIExploitation High
Alerts when the x-ghost-preview header arrives with no session cookie present — the exact unauthenticated-attacker precondition the advisory calls out. Legitimate preview traffic carries a Ghost staff session; an anonymous request setting this header is an exploitation attempt against the shared cache. Rationale: Combines the advisory's exact header token with its stated precondition ('an unauthenticated user could send an x-ghost-preview header') by requiring absence of any Ghost session cookie, which cleanly separates malicious anonymous abuse from legit authenticated preview. Datadog/Sigma omitted — reliable cookie-absence negation is not expressible on free-text syslog or single-selection Sigma. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch omitted (no HTTP header telemetry). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized penetration test or bug-bounty researcher probing the CVE
  • CDN misconfiguration that strips cookies before logging
  • Internal QA script deliberately exercising preview without login
  • Anonymized/privacy-proxy traffic that removes cookie headers before the WAF
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the request had no valid Ghost staff session and identify the source IP/ASN and the targeted URL. A single anonymous host repeatedly setting x-ghost-preview across multiple URLs is high-confidence exploitation. 2) Contain: apply the cache-layer workaround (bypass cache on x-ghost-preview) immediately, block the offending source at the WAF, and confirm/schedule upgrade to Ghost >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: enumerate every URL this source touched, check the cache for poisoned entries, and review staff-account activity on the frontend domain; if credential compromise is suspected use Ghost's 'Reset all authentication' (>=6.41.0).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| where isempty(RequestCookies) or RequestCookies !has "ghost"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestCookies, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
index=web OR index=proxy (sourcetype="nginx:plus:access" OR sourcetype="nginx:access" OR sourcetype="access_combined" OR sourcetype="cloudflare:json" OR sourcetype="fastly") "x-ghost-preview"
| search NOT _raw="*Cookie:*" AND NOT _raw="*ghost-admin-api-session*"
| stats count as hits, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(uri_path) as uri_path by host, clientip
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - hits
Ghost x-ghost-preview request carrying XSS payload markers (CVE-2026-53943 execution) AIExploitation High
Alerts when an x-ghost-preview request also contains HTML/JavaScript injection markers — the actual XSS payload that CVE-2026-53943 renders into the frontend response and stores in the shared cache to be served to subsequent visitors. Pairs the vulnerability trigger with the malicious content in one event. Rationale: Correlates the advisory's exact vulnerability trigger (x-ghost-preview) with classic reflected/stored XSS markers in the same request, capturing the injected content that gets rendered and cached ('served to subsequent visitors'). Very low FP because a preview request AND a script payload together has no benign explanation. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch omitted — no HTTP payload telemetry in those sources. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/ghost/CVE-2026-53943/ • https://dailycve.com/ghost-cms-cache-poisoning-xss-cve-2026-53943-critical-dc-jul2026-821/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated web vulnerability scanner (Burp/Acunetix/Nuclei) firing XSS probes with the preview header
  • Authorized penetration test validating CVE-2026-53943
  • WAF already blocked the request but still logged it (check DeviceAction/Activity)
  • Legitimate blog content whose title/body genuinely contains the literal string '<script' in a code sample
Suppression filter
| where DeviceAction != "blocked" and DeviceAction != "deny"
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the injected payload from the request and the target URL; confirm whether the WAF blocked or passed it, and whether the response was subsequently cached and served (cache HIT) to other clients. 2) Contain: purge the affected URL(s) from the shared cache, apply the x-ghost-preview cache-bypass workaround, block the source IP, and verify Ghost is >=6.37.0. 3) Hunt: search staff logons on the frontend domain and any admin-session cookies for signs of takeover, review all URLs the source touched, and if compromise is confirmed invoke Ghost 'Reset all authentication' (>=6.41.0).
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| where Message has_any ("<script", "onerror=", "onload=", "javascript:", "<svg", "<img", "%3Cscript", "document.cookie")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fleet valuesFrom cross-namespace secret/configmap reference (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts Rancher Fleet GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle custom resources whose spec contains a `valuesFrom` block with a secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef, the exact mechanism CVE-2026-44935 abuses to read secrets in namespaces the tenant is not authorized for. Article-specific because it pivots on the Fleet CRD resource names plus the `valuesFrom` key-reference structure rather than generic secret access. Rationale: Uses the exact Fleet CRD resource names (gitrepos/helmops/bundles from go:github.com/rancher/fleet) and the `valuesFrom` + secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef structure named in GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x as the exploitation vector; high-fidelity because legitimate fleet.yaml normally references secrets in the same namespace only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-namespace GitOps deployment where an operator intentionally references a shared config namespace
  • Fleet platform team testing valuesFrom against a sanctioned central secrets namespace
  • CI pipelines that template Bundles with valuesFrom to a common values ConfigMap
  • Upgrade migrations that recreate existing GitRepo resources with unchanged valuesFrom blocks
Suppression filter
| where not (Username has "system:serviceaccount:cattle-fleet-system" and ObjNamespace == extract(@"namespace:\s*([a-z0-9-]+)", 1, ReqStr))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RequestObject; compare the namespace inside valuesFrom to ObjectRef.namespace and to the tenant that owns the requesting Username — a mismatch to a namespace the tenant has no RBAC in is the true positive. 2) Contain: delete/suspend the offending GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle, and rotate any secret whose name/namespace/key appears in the valuesFrom reference (advisory explicitly recommends rotation). 3) Hunt: enumerate all Fleet CRs created by the same Username across the cluster and check whether the Fleet agent service account subsequently read those referenced secrets (see companion fan-out UC).
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend ObjResource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), ObjNamespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)
| where ObjResource in ("gitrepos","helmops","bundles")
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where ReqStr has "valuesFrom" and (ReqStr has "secretKeyRef" or ReqStr has "configMapKeyRef")
| where ReqStr has "namespace"    // cross-namespace ref requires an explicit namespace inside valuesFrom
| project TimeGenerated, Username, Verb, ObjResource, ObjNamespace, RequestUri, ReqStr
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fleet agent service account reads secrets across multiple namespaces (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the downstream-cluster fingerprint of CVE-2026-44935: the Fleet agent service account issuing get/list of secrets or configmaps across an abnormal number of distinct namespaces within a short window, indicating cross-tenant credential harvesting via unrestricted valuesFrom/HelmOp deployment. Article-specific because it keys on the Fleet agent SA identity and the cross-namespace fan-out the advisory tells defenders to review logs for. Rationale: Pivots on the Fleet agent service account identity (cattle-fleet-system fleet-agent) reading secrets/configmaps across namespaces — the exact post-exploit behaviour GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x tells operators to review cluster logs for and to drive credential rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007 T1613
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-tenant cluster where the Fleet agent SA is authorized to deploy into many namespaces by design
  • Initial Fleet onboarding/bootstrap that syncs bundles into a large set of namespaces at once
  • Backup/DR tooling running under a fleet-labelled SA enumerating secrets
  • Cluster-wide chart rollout (e.g. cert-manager, monitoring) driven through Fleet touching every namespace
Response runbook
1) Triage: list the distinct namespaces and secret names the Fleet agent SA touched; confirm against the tenant boundary — reads into namespaces owned by a different tenant are the true positive. 2) Contain: rotate the Fleet agent service account token and every secret it read cross-tenant, then apply the patched-version Policy resource pinning a least-privilege service account per GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle namespace. 3) Hunt: correlate back to companion UC (valuesFrom cross-namespace references) to identify which GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle CR triggered the reads and which tenant Username authored it; upgrade Fleet to v0.15.2/v0.14.6/0.13.11/v0.12.15.

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Rancher /v3/import authImage YAML injection via URL-encoded newlines (CVE-2026-44939) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound web requests to the Rancher cluster-import endpoint /v3/import/{token}_{clusterId}.yaml where the authImage query parameter carries URL-encoded newlines (%0A/%0D) or raw newlines — the exact YAML-breakout primitive used to inject arbitrary manifest keys. Article-specific because it keys on the concrete endpoint path plus the authImage parameter plus the newline breakout characters, not a generic web attack. Rationale: Uses the exact article strings: endpoint '/v3/import/', parameter 'authImage', and the URL-encoded newline breakout (%0A/%0D) named as the patch target. Legitimate agent-image overrides never contain newline encodings, so FP rate is very low. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44939 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/rancher/rancher/CVE-2026-44939/ • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-44939
ATT&CKT1190 T1610
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security scanners (Nessus/Nuclei) probing the /v3/import endpoint with crafted payloads during authorized pentests
  • Rancher agent troubleshooting where an operator manually URL-encodes an image tag containing a '+' or ':' (rare, and won't include %0A/%0D)
  • WAF/proxy that double-decodes and re-logs the query string, producing a benign echoed value
  • Automated CI that templates import URLs and accidentally embeds a trailing whitespace character
Suppression filter
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","nuclei","Nuclei","masscan")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RequestURL and URL-decode the authImage value; confirm it contains newline bytes followed by injected YAML keys (command:, hostPath, hostNetwork). Note SourceIP and whether the request returned 200. 2) Contain: block the SourceIP at the WAF, invalidate/rotate the affected cluster registration token, and confirm Rancher is on a patched build (>= 2.14.2/2.13.6/2.12.10/2.11.14/2.10.12). 3) Hunt: pivot to Kubernetes audit logs for any DaemonSet create/update in cattle-system named kube-api-auth carrying command:/args:, and search endpoints for kubectl apply of the same import URL.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/v3/import/"
| where RequestURL has "authImage"
| where RequestURL has_any ("%0A","%0a","%0D","%0d","%0d%0a","\n","\r")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, ReceivedBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
